q: A CodePipeline V2 type pipeline has a source stage with CodeCommit, a build stage with CodeBuild, and a deploy stage with CodeDeploy. The pipeline fails at the build stage. What happens to the deploy stage?

opts.a: The deploy stage runs with the last successful build artifact
opts.b: The deploy stage is skipped and the pipeline execution fails
opts.c: The deploy stage runs with an empty artifact
opts.d: The pipeline retries the build stage automatically 3 times before failing

exp.a: Incorrect. CodePipeline does not use previous artifacts for the current execution.
exp.b: Correct. If any stage fails, subsequent stages are not executed and the entire pipeline execution is marked as failed.
exp.c: Incorrect. The deploy stage will not execute at all.
exp.d: Incorrect. CodePipeline does not automatically retry failed stages.

q: Your CodeBuild project uses a buildspec.yml that references AWS Secrets Manager for database credentials. The build fails with an access denied error. What is the most likely cause?

opts.a: Secrets Manager is not available in the build region
opts.b: The CodeBuild service role lacks permission to access the secret
opts.c: buildspec.yml does not support Secrets Manager references
opts.d: The secret must be stored in Parameter Store instead

exp.a: Incorrect. Secrets Manager is available in all regions where CodeBuild operates.
exp.b: Correct. The CodeBuild service role must have secretsmanager:GetSecretValue permission for the specific secret ARN.
exp.c: Incorrect. buildspec.yml supports Secrets Manager references in the env/secrets-manager section.
exp.d: Incorrect. CodeBuild supports both Secrets Manager and Parameter Store.

q: A team has configured a CodeDeploy Blue/Green deployment for EC2 instances. After the new environment is validated, how long does CodeDeploy wait by default before terminating the original instances?

opts.a: Immediately after traffic rerouting
opts.b: 1 hour
opts.c: The wait time is configurable in the deployment group (default is 0 minutes if set to terminate immediately, or up to specified wait time)

exp.a: Incorrect. The behavior depends on the deployment group configuration.
exp.b: Incorrect. 1 hour is not a fixed default.
exp.c: Correct. The termination wait time is configurable in the deployment group. You can set it to terminate immediately, keep original instances, or wait a specified duration (up to 2880 minutes/48 hours).
exp.d: Incorrect. 24 hours is not the default.

q: A CodePipeline uses a cross-account deployment. The pipeline in Account A needs to deploy using CodeDeploy in Account B. What must be configured?

opts.a: Only a VPC peering connection between the accounts
opts.b: A cross-account IAM role in Account B that the pipeline role in Account A can assume, plus a KMS key policy for artifact encryption
opts.c: AWS Organizations SCP allowing deployment
opts.d: A shared S3 bucket in a third account

exp.a: Incorrect. VPC peering is for network connectivity, not IAM permissions.
exp.b: Correct. Cross-account CodePipeline requires a cross-account role in the target account with trust policy for the source account, and the KMS key used for artifact encryption must grant access to the target account.
exp.c: Incorrect. SCPs restrict permissions but don't enable cross-account deployment alone.
exp.d: Incorrect. While artifact stores matter, a third account bucket is not the requirement.

q: Your CodeBuild project builds successfully but the output artifacts are not appearing in the expected S3 location. Which section of buildspec.yml should you check?

opts.a: phases/post_build
opts.b: artifacts
opts.c: env

exp.a: Incorrect. post_build runs commands but doesn't define artifact locations.
exp.b: Correct. The artifacts section in buildspec.yml defines the files to include, the base directory, and the discard-paths setting for output artifacts.
exp.c: Incorrect. The env section defines environment variables, not artifact configuration.
exp.d: Incorrect. The install phase installs dependencies, not artifact configuration.

q: What is the maximum build timeout that can be configured for a CodeBuild project?

opts.a: 1 hour
opts.b: 8 hours (480 minutes)
opts.c: 24 hours

exp.a: Incorrect. 1 hour is below the maximum.
exp.b: Correct. The maximum build timeout for a CodeBuild project is 8 hours (480 minutes). The minimum is 5 minutes and the default is 60 minutes.
exp.c: Incorrect. 24 hours exceeds the maximum allowed.
exp.d: Incorrect. 12 hours exceeds the 8-hour maximum.

q: What is the minimum build timeout that can be configured for a CodeBuild project?

opts.a: 1 minute
opts.b: 5 minutes
opts.c: 10 minutes

exp.a: Incorrect. 1 minute is below the minimum allowed.
exp.b: Correct. The minimum build timeout for CodeBuild is 5 minutes.
exp.c: Incorrect. The minimum is lower than 10 minutes.
exp.d: Incorrect. 15 minutes is above the minimum allowed.

q: A team wants to run CodeBuild builds concurrently but is hitting throttling. What is the default concurrent build limit per account?

exp.a: Incorrect. The default is higher than 10.
exp.b: Incorrect. 20 is below the default limit.
exp.c: Correct. The default concurrent build limit is 60 per account. This can be increased via Service Quotas.
exp.d: Incorrect. 100 exceeds the default (though it can be increased).

q: A company has a CodeDeploy deployment that uses the AllAtOnce deployment configuration for a fleet of 10 EC2 instances. The deployment fails on 3 instances. What is the deployment result?

opts.a: Deployment succeeds because majority (7/10) succeeded
opts.b: Deployment fails because AllAtOnce requires all instances to succeed
opts.c: Deployment succeeds because AllAtOnce only requires one instance to succeed for the overall deployment to succeed
opts.d: Deployment is rolled back automatically to all instances

exp.a: Incorrect. AllAtOnce doesn't use majority logic.
exp.b: Incorrect. AllAtOnce does not require all instances to succeed.
exp.c: Correct. With CodeDeployDefault.AllAtOnce, the overall deployment succeeds if the application revision is deployed to at least one instance. The deployment fails only if it fails on all instances.
exp.d: Incorrect. Automatic rollback depends on deployment group configuration, not the deployment configuration alone.

q: In a CodeDeploy HalfAtATime deployment with 10 instances, how many instances must successfully deploy for the overall deployment to be considered successful?

opts.a: All 10 instances
opts.b: At least 5 instances
opts.c: At least 6 instances

exp.a: Incorrect. HalfAtATime doesn't require all instances.
exp.b: Correct. With HalfAtATime, CodeDeploy deploys to up to half the instances at a time (rounded down). The overall deployment succeeds if at least half succeed.
exp.c: Incorrect. The minimum success threshold is half (5 out of 10).
exp.d: Incorrect. 8 is above the minimum requirement.

q: In CodeBuild, what is the purpose of the 'reports' section in buildspec.yml?

opts.a: To generate billing reports
opts.b: To publish test results and code coverage reports to CodeBuild report groups
opts.c: To send email notifications about build status

exp.a: Incorrect. The reports section is not for billing.
exp.b: Correct. The reports section allows you to specify test result files (JUnit, NUnit, Cucumber, etc.) and code coverage files that CodeBuild publishes to report groups for visualization.
exp.c: Incorrect. Notifications are configured separately, not in the reports section.
exp.d: Incorrect. CloudWatch metrics are published automatically, not through the reports section.

q: A team has a monorepo in CodeCommit with multiple microservices. They want different pipelines triggered by changes in specific directories. How should they configure this?

opts.a: Create separate branches for each microservice
opts.b: Use CodePipeline trigger filters with file path conditions in the EventBridge rule
opts.c: Create one pipeline that deploys all services every time

exp.a: Incorrect. Separate branches add complexity and don't solve the trigger problem.
exp.b: Correct. CodePipeline V2 type supports trigger filters that can include/exclude file paths, allowing specific pipelines to trigger only when files in designated directories change.
exp.c: Incorrect. Deploying all services on every change is wasteful.
exp.d: Incorrect. Batch builds run multiple builds but don't solve pipeline triggering.

q: What is the difference between CodePipeline V1 and V2 pipeline types?

opts.a: V2 only supports CodeCommit as a source
opts.b: V2 supports triggers with filtering, pipeline-level variables, and Git tags; V1 charges per pipeline per month while V2 charges per action execution
opts.c: V1 is deprecated and no longer available
opts.d: V2 does not support manual approvals

exp.a: Incorrect. V2 supports all source providers.
exp.b: Correct. V2 introduces triggers with filtering (branch, file path, tags), pipeline-level variables, Git tags as triggers, and uses action-execution-based pricing rather than per-pipeline-per-month.
exp.c: Incorrect. V1 pipelines still exist and can be created.
exp.d: Incorrect. V2 supports all action types including manual approvals.

q: Your CodeBuild project needs to access a private Maven repository hosted on an EC2 instance in a private subnet. The build fails with a connection timeout. What should you configure?

opts.a: Enable privileged mode in CodeBuild
opts.b: Configure the CodeBuild project with VPC settings (VPC ID, private subnet, and security group) that allow access to the Maven repository
opts.c: Add the Maven repository URL to the buildspec.yml env section
opts.d: Create a NAT Gateway in the public subnet

exp.a: Incorrect. Privileged mode is for Docker builds, not VPC access.
exp.b: Correct. CodeBuild must be configured with VPC settings to access resources in private subnets. The security group must allow outbound traffic to the Maven repository.
exp.c: Incorrect. Adding the URL doesn't solve network connectivity issues.
exp.d: Incorrect. A NAT Gateway alone won't help unless CodeBuild is configured to run in the VPC.

q: A CodeBuild project configured with VPC access cannot pull dependencies from the internet. What is the likely issue?

opts.a: The buildspec.yml is missing the install phase
opts.b: The VPC subnet has no route to a NAT Gateway or VPC endpoints for internet access
opts.c: CodeBuild doesn't support internet access when in a VPC
opts.d: The IAM role is missing S3 permissions

exp.a: Incorrect. The install phase doesn't affect network connectivity.
exp.b: Correct. When CodeBuild runs in a VPC, it uses the VPC's networking. The subnet must have a route to a NAT Gateway (for internet) or appropriate VPC endpoints for AWS services.
exp.c: Incorrect. Internet access is possible via NAT Gateway when CodeBuild is in a VPC.
exp.d: Incorrect. While IAM permissions matter, network connectivity is the primary issue here.

q: What is the maximum number of CodeDeploy deployment groups per application?

exp.a: Incorrect. The limit is higher than 10.
exp.b: Correct. CodeDeploy allows a maximum of 25 deployment groups per application by default.
exp.c: Incorrect. 100 exceeds the default limit.
exp.d: Incorrect. 1,000 is the limit for applications per account, not deployment groups per application.

q: What is the maximum number of CodeDeploy applications per account per region?

exp.a: Incorrect. The limit is higher than 100.
exp.b: Incorrect. 500 is below the actual limit.
exp.c: Correct. CodeDeploy allows a maximum of 1,000 applications per account per region.
exp.d: Incorrect. 5,000 exceeds the default limit.

q: A company uses CodeDeploy with EC2 instances behind an Elastic Load Balancer. During deployment, they want instances to be deregistered from the load balancer before deployment and re-registered after. Which lifecycle hooks handle this?

opts.a: BeforeInstall and AfterInstall
opts.b: BeforeBlockTraffic and AfterAllowTraffic
opts.c: ApplicationStop and ApplicationStart

exp.a: Incorrect. These hooks don't manage load balancer traffic.
exp.b: Correct. BeforeBlockTraffic runs before instances are deregistered from the load balancer, and AfterAllowTraffic runs after instances are re-registered. BlockTraffic and AllowTraffic are the actual deregistration/registration events.
exp.c: Incorrect. These manage application lifecycle, not load balancer traffic.
exp.d: Incorrect. These are internal CodeDeploy events, not configurable hooks.

q: What is the correct order of CodeDeploy lifecycle hooks for an in-place deployment?

opts.a: Install → BeforeInstall → AfterInstall → ApplicationStart
opts.b: ApplicationStop → DownloadBundle → BeforeInstall → Install → AfterInstall → ApplicationStart → ValidateService
opts.c: BeforeInstall → Install → ApplicationStart → ValidateService

exp.a: Incorrect. This order is wrong; BeforeInstall must come before Install.
exp.b: Correct. The complete lifecycle order is: ApplicationStop → DownloadBundle → BeforeInstall → Install → AfterInstall → ApplicationStart → ValidateService.
exp.c: Incorrect. This is incomplete; it's missing ApplicationStop and DownloadBundle.
exp.d: Incorrect. AfterInstall must come before ApplicationStart.

q: A developer pushes code to CodeCommit which triggers CodePipeline. The pipeline source action detects the change but shows the wrong commit. What is the likely cause?

opts.a: The pipeline was triggered by a different branch than expected
opts.b: CodeCommit has a caching issue
opts.c: The EventBridge rule has a delay
opts.d: CodePipeline only checks for changes every 5 minutes

exp.a: Correct. If the pipeline is configured to monitor a specific branch but the EventBridge rule triggers on any branch change, it may pick up changes from an unexpected branch. Verify the branch configuration in the source action.
exp.b: Incorrect. CodeCommit doesn't have caching issues that cause wrong commits.
exp.c: Incorrect. EventBridge delivers events in near real-time.
exp.d: Incorrect. V2 pipelines with EventBridge triggers don't use polling.

q: Your CodeBuild project needs to publish a Docker image to ECR but fails with 'no basic auth credentials'. What is missing?

opts.a: The buildspec.yml is missing the artifacts section
opts.b: The pre_build phase should include an ECR login command (aws ecr get-login-password) and the service role needs ecr:GetAuthorizationToken permission
opts.c: Docker Hub credentials need to be configured

exp.a: Incorrect. The artifacts section is unrelated to ECR authentication.
exp.b: Correct. You must authenticate to ECR before pushing images. The pre_build phase should run 'aws ecr get-login-password | docker login' and the IAM role needs ecr:GetAuthorizationToken, ecr:BatchCheckLayerAvailability, ecr:PutImage, etc.
exp.c: Incorrect. Docker Hub credentials are not needed for ECR.
exp.d: Incorrect. A non-existent repository would give a different error.

q: What is CodeBuild's 'batch build' feature used for?

opts.a: Running a single build faster using multiple CPUs
opts.b: Running multiple builds in a single build project with defined dependencies, fan-out, or build matrix configurations
opts.c: Queuing builds for overnight processing

exp.a: Incorrect. Batch builds use multiple build environments, not multiple CPUs in one.
exp.b: Correct. Batch builds allow you to define multiple builds in a single project using build-list (parallel), build-graph (dependencies), or build-matrix (combinations) configurations.
exp.c: Incorrect. Batch builds run immediately, not queued for later.
exp.d: Incorrect. Automatic retry is a separate feature from batch builds.

q: A team uses CodePipeline with a manual approval stage before production deployment. The approver is on vacation and the approval times out. What is the default timeout for a manual approval action?

opts.a: 24 hours
opts.b: 7 days
opts.c: 30 days

exp.a: Incorrect. Manual approval actions have a longer timeout.
exp.b: Correct. Manual approval actions in CodePipeline have a default timeout of 7 days. If not approved or rejected within 7 days, the action times out and the pipeline execution fails.
exp.c: Incorrect. 30 days exceeds the actual timeout.
exp.d: Incorrect. Manual approval actions do have a timeout.

q: Your team uses CodeBuild with S3 caching to speed up builds. After changing the build environment image, the cache is not being used. Why?

opts.a: S3 caching doesn't work with different build images
opts.b: The cache key is derived from the buildspec and environment; changing the image may invalidate the cache path or the cached dependencies are incompatible
opts.c: S3 caching only works with the first build image configured
opts.d: You must manually clear and rebuild the cache

exp.a: Incorrect. S3 caching works with different images, but the cache content may be incompatible.
exp.b: Correct. When you change the build environment image, the cached dependencies (e.g., different OS package versions) may be incompatible, effectively making the cache unusable for the new environment.
exp.c: Incorrect. S3 caching works with any build image.
exp.d: Incorrect. While clearing the cache is an option, the root cause is cache incompatibility.

q: What is the maximum number of webhooks per CodePipeline per region?

exp.a: Incorrect. The limit is much higher than 10.
exp.b: Incorrect. 50 is below the actual limit.
exp.c: Incorrect. 150 is below the limit.
exp.d: Correct. CodePipeline allows up to 300 webhooks per region per account.

q: A CodeDeploy deployment to Lambda uses CodeDeployDefault.LambdaLinear10PercentEvery1Minute. If the Lambda function handles 1000 requests/minute, approximately how many requests hit the new version after 3 minutes?

opts.a: 100 requests
opts.b: 300 requests
opts.c: 500 requests

exp.a: Incorrect. After 3 minutes, 30% of traffic goes to the new version.
exp.b: Correct. Linear10PercentEvery1Minute shifts 10% per minute. After 3 minutes, 30% of traffic (300 out of 1000 requests) goes to the new version.
exp.c: Incorrect. 50% would be after 5 minutes.
exp.d: Incorrect. All traffic shifts only after 10 minutes.

q: A CodeDeploy deployment uses LambdaCanary10Percent5Minutes. What happens if an error is detected during the initial 5-minute monitoring period?

opts.a: Deployment continues regardless
opts.b: All traffic is immediately shifted to the new version
opts.c: The deployment is rolled back and 100% of traffic returns to the original version
opts.d: Traffic is split 50/50 for additional testing

exp.a: Incorrect. Errors trigger rollback if alarms are configured.
exp.b: Incorrect. Errors don't accelerate deployment.
exp.c: Correct. If CloudWatch alarms trigger during the canary period, CodeDeploy automatically rolls back, returning all traffic to the original Lambda version.
exp.d: Incorrect. There is no intermediate 50/50 state in canary deployments.

q: Which CodeBuild feature allows you to run multiple build commands on different compute types simultaneously?

opts.a: Parallel phases
opts.b: Batch builds with build-matrix
opts.c: Multi-stage builds

exp.a: Incorrect. Phases run sequentially within a single build.
exp.b: Correct. Batch builds with build-matrix allow you to define combinations of environment variables, images, and compute types that run as separate builds simultaneously.
exp.c: Incorrect. Multi-stage builds are a Docker concept, not CodeBuild.
exp.d: Incorrect. Concurrent projects are separate projects, not coordinated matrix builds.

q: A team configures CodePipeline with two source actions: CodeCommit and S3. Under what condition does the pipeline execute?

opts.a: Only when both sources change simultaneously
opts.b: When either source detects a change
opts.c: Only when CodeCommit changes (primary source)
opts.d: On a scheduled basis regardless of changes

exp.a: Incorrect. Both sources don't need to change simultaneously.
exp.b: Correct. When a pipeline has multiple source actions, a change detected in any source action triggers the pipeline execution.
exp.c: Incorrect. Both sources can independently trigger the pipeline.
exp.d: Incorrect. CodePipeline triggers on source changes, not schedules (unless specifically configured).

q: What is the maximum size of the CodePipeline artifact stored in S3?

opts.a: 256 MB
opts.b: 512 MB
opts.c: 1 GB

exp.a: Incorrect. The limit is larger than 256 MB.
exp.b: Correct. The maximum size of artifacts in a source or build action in CodePipeline is 512 MB.
exp.c: Incorrect. 1 GB exceeds the limit.
exp.d: Incorrect. 5 GB is far above the limit.

q: A CodeDeploy in-place deployment is configured with automatic rollback on deployment failure. During rollback, what actually happens?

opts.a: CodeDeploy undoes the changes made by the failed deployment
opts.b: CodeDeploy creates a new deployment that deploys the last known good revision
opts.c: The EC2 instances are terminated and replaced
opts.d: CodeDeploy restores from an EBS snapshot

exp.a: Incorrect. CodeDeploy doesn't reverse individual changes.
exp.b: Correct. During a rollback, CodeDeploy creates a new deployment that deploys the last known good application revision to the deployment group. It's a forward deployment of the previous version.
exp.c: Incorrect. In-place deployments don't terminate instances.
exp.d: Incorrect. EBS snapshots are not used in CodeDeploy rollbacks.

q: Your CodeBuild project produces build artifacts that need to be used by multiple subsequent CodePipeline stages. How should the artifacts be configured?

opts.a: Upload to S3 manually in post_build
opts.b: Define multiple output artifacts in the CodeBuild action configuration using secondary-artifacts in buildspec.yml
opts.c: Use a single artifact and duplicate it in each stage

exp.a: Incorrect. Manual S3 upload bypasses CodePipeline's artifact management.
exp.b: Correct. CodeBuild supports secondary-artifacts in buildspec.yml, and CodePipeline can map these as output artifacts for consumption by multiple downstream stages.
exp.c: Incorrect. Duplicating artifacts is unnecessary with proper configuration.
exp.d: Incorrect. DynamoDB is not used for build artifact storage.

q: What is the maximum number of concurrent deployments per deployment group in CodeDeploy?

exp.a: Correct. CodeDeploy allows only 1 active deployment per deployment group at a time. If a new deployment is triggered while one is in progress, the new deployment may either queue or replace the current one depending on configuration.
exp.b: Incorrect. Only 1 deployment can be active per group.
exp.c: Incorrect. The limit is 1.
exp.d: Incorrect. There is a limit of 1 active deployment per group.

q: A team wants to use CodeBuild to run integration tests against a database. They need the database to be available only during the build. What approach should they use?

opts.a: Launch an RDS instance before each build
opts.b: Use CodeBuild's support for Docker Compose or sidecar containers to spin up a test database during the build
opts.c: Use a shared production database
opts.d: Store database data in the build cache

exp.a: Incorrect. Launching RDS for each build is slow and expensive.
exp.b: Correct. CodeBuild with privileged mode can run Docker Compose to start sidecar containers (like a test database) during the build, which are destroyed after the build completes.
exp.c: Incorrect. Using production databases for testing is risky.
exp.d: Incorrect. Database data cannot be meaningfully stored in build cache.

q: What is the purpose of the 'fileExistsBehavior' setting in CodeDeploy?

opts.a: It determines how to handle files that already exist on the target instance during deployment
opts.b: It specifies whether to compress files during transfer
opts.c: It controls file permissions after deployment
opts.d: It determines the file encoding format

exp.a: Correct. fileExistsBehavior can be set to DISALLOW (fail if file exists), OVERWRITE (replace existing files), or RETAIN (keep existing files). This applies during in-place deployments.
exp.b: Incorrect. File compression is not controlled by this setting.
exp.c: Incorrect. File permissions are handled in lifecycle hook scripts.
exp.d: Incorrect. File encoding is not related to this setting.

q: A team uses CodePipeline V2 and wants to trigger the pipeline only when changes are pushed to the 'main' branch and only when files in the 'src/' directory are modified. How is this configured?

opts.a: Using Lambda trigger function to filter changes
opts.b: Using pipeline trigger filters with branch include pattern 'main' and file path include pattern 'src/**'
opts.c: Creating a separate repository for src/ files
opts.d: Using EventBridge rules with custom pattern matching

exp.a: Incorrect. Lambda functions are not needed for this built-in feature.
exp.b: Correct. CodePipeline V2 supports trigger filters that allow branch filtering and file path filtering directly in the pipeline configuration.
exp.c: Incorrect. Separating repositories adds unnecessary complexity.
exp.d: Incorrect. While EventBridge triggers pipelines, V2 pipeline trigger filters provide native file path filtering.

q: Your CodeDeploy deployment to ECS using Blue/Green fails during the AfterAllowTestTraffic hook. What happens?

opts.a: Production traffic is shifted to the new task set
opts.b: The deployment rolls back: the original task set continues serving production traffic and the replacement task set is terminated
opts.c: Both task sets continue running indefinitely
opts.d: The ECS service is stopped completely

exp.a: Incorrect. A hook failure prevents traffic shifting.
exp.b: Correct. If any lifecycle hook fails during an ECS Blue/Green deployment, the deployment fails and rolls back. The original task set retains production traffic and the replacement is terminated.
exp.c: Incorrect. Failed deployments don't leave both running permanently.
exp.d: Incorrect. The ECS service continues with the original task set.

q: What authentication methods does CodeCommit support for Git operations?

opts.a: Only HTTPS with username and password
opts.b: SSH keys, HTTPS Git credentials, and HTTPS via AWS CLI credential helper
opts.c: Only SSH keys

exp.a: Incorrect. CodeCommit supports multiple authentication methods.
exp.b: Correct. CodeCommit supports SSH keys (uploaded to IAM), HTTPS Git credentials (generated in IAM), and the AWS CLI credential helper (uses IAM credentials/temporary credentials).
exp.c: Incorrect. Multiple methods are supported beyond SSH.
exp.d: Incorrect. OAuth tokens are not the authentication mechanism for CodeCommit.

q: A team wants to enforce that all CodeCommit pull requests pass CodeBuild tests before merging. How should they configure this?

opts.a: Use a Lambda function to block merges
opts.b: Configure an approval rule template requiring a successful CodeBuild approval
opts.c: Use CodePipeline to run tests on every pull request
opts.d: Configure branch permissions and add a CodeBuild trigger on pull request events with approval rules

exp.a: Incorrect. While possible, this is not the native approach.
exp.b: Incorrect. Approval rule templates require human approvals, not automated build approvals.
exp.c: Incorrect. CodePipeline doesn't natively run on pull request events.
exp.d: Correct. You configure CodeCommit notification rules or EventBridge to trigger CodeBuild on pull request events, and use approval rules that prevent merging until conditions are met.

q: What is the maximum number of approval rules per pull request in CodeCommit?

exp.a: Incorrect. The limit is higher.
exp.b: Incorrect. 10 is below the actual limit.
exp.c: Incorrect. The limit is slightly higher.
exp.d: Correct. CodeCommit allows a maximum of 30 approval rules per pull request (combined from approval rule templates and individual rules).

q: A company wants to deploy the same application to both staging and production accounts using CodePipeline. The pipeline exists in a central DevOps account. What architecture pattern should they use?

opts.a: Create separate pipelines in each account
opts.b: Use a single pipeline with cross-account roles, CMK key policies granting access to target accounts, and cross-account S3 bucket policies
opts.c: Copy artifacts manually between accounts
opts.d: Use AWS RAM to share the pipeline

exp.a: Incorrect. Separate pipelines don't provide centralized control.
exp.b: Correct. Cross-account CodePipeline uses IAM roles in target accounts, KMS key policies allowing target accounts to decrypt artifacts, and S3 bucket policies allowing target accounts access.
exp.c: Incorrect. Manual artifact copying defeats the purpose of CI/CD automation.
exp.d: Incorrect. CodePipeline cannot be shared via AWS RAM.

q: In CodeBuild, what does the 'queued timeout' setting control?

opts.a: How long a build can run before being terminated
opts.b: How long a build can wait in the queue before the build project is removed
opts.c: How long before artifacts expire
opts.d: How long to wait for source code download

exp.a: Incorrect. That's the build timeout, not queued timeout.
exp.b: Correct. The queued timeout specifies how long a build can remain in the queue waiting for available compute resources. Default is 8 hours, maximum is 8 hours.
exp.c: Incorrect. Artifact expiration is not controlled by queued timeout.
exp.d: Incorrect. Source code download time is part of the build execution.

q: A CodePipeline execution starts but a new commit is pushed before the current execution completes. What happens with the V2 pipeline type?

opts.a: The new commit is ignored until the current execution completes
opts.b: The current execution is superseded by the newer execution
opts.c: Both executions run simultaneously through all stages
opts.d: The pipeline fails with a conflict error

exp.a: Incorrect. V2 pipelines don't ignore new changes.
exp.b: Correct. In V2 pipelines with SUPERSEDED execution mode, a newer execution supersedes the older one. The older execution is stopped and replaced by the newer one when it reaches the same stage.
exp.c: Incorrect. Pipelines don't run multiple executions through the same stage simultaneously by default.
exp.d: Incorrect. There's no conflict error; superseding is expected behavior.

q: What execution modes are available for CodePipeline V2 type?

opts.a: Sequential only
opts.b: SUPERSEDED, QUEUED, and PARALLEL
opts.c: FIFO and LIFO

exp.a: Incorrect. Multiple execution modes are available.
exp.b: Correct. V2 pipelines support SUPERSEDED (newer replaces older), QUEUED (executions run one at a time in order), and PARALLEL (all executions run independently).
exp.c: Incorrect. FIFO/LIFO are not CodePipeline execution mode names.
exp.d: Incorrect. These are not valid execution mode names.

q: Your team needs every pipeline execution to complete without being superseded. Which execution mode should you configure?

opts.a: SUPERSEDED
opts.b: PARALLEL
opts.c: QUEUED

exp.a: Incorrect. SUPERSEDED allows newer executions to replace older ones.
exp.b: Incorrect. PARALLEL runs all executions simultaneously but doesn't guarantee each one completes the full pipeline independently.
exp.c: Correct. QUEUED mode ensures each execution runs to completion one at a time in order, so no execution is superseded.
exp.d: Incorrect. SEQUENTIAL is not a valid execution mode name.

q: A team wants to use CodeBuild to run tests for pull requests in GitHub without triggering the full CodePipeline. What should they use?

opts.a: CodePipeline source action with GitHub webhook
opts.b: CodeBuild project with GitHub webhook trigger configured for PULL_REQUEST_CREATED and PULL_REQUEST_UPDATED events
opts.c: Lambda function polling GitHub API

exp.a: Incorrect. This triggers the full pipeline, not just tests.
exp.b: Correct. CodeBuild can be directly triggered by GitHub webhooks for specific events (PULL_REQUEST_CREATED, PULL_REQUEST_UPDATED, PULL_REQUEST_REOPENED) without needing CodePipeline.
exp.c: Incorrect. Polling is inefficient and not the recommended approach.
exp.d: Incorrect. Mirroring doesn't help with PR-specific testing.

q: What is the maximum number of tags per CodeDeploy resource?

exp.a: Incorrect. The limit is higher.
exp.b: Incorrect. 25 is below the actual limit.
exp.c: Correct. CodeDeploy resources support a maximum of 50 tags per resource.
exp.d: Incorrect. 200 exceeds the actual limit.

q: Your CodeDeploy deployment to EC2 uses an Auto Scaling group. A scale-out event occurs during deployment. What happens to the new instances?

opts.a: New instances don't receive the deployment
opts.b: New instances receive the last successfully deployed revision, not the in-progress deployment
opts.c: New instances receive the in-progress deployment

exp.a: Incorrect. CodeDeploy does deploy to new instances.
exp.b: Correct. When an Auto Scaling scale-out event occurs during a deployment, CodeDeploy deploys the last successfully deployed revision to the new instances, not the revision currently being deployed.
exp.c: Incorrect. The in-progress revision is not deployed to new instances.
exp.d: Incorrect. The deployment continues; new instances get the last successful revision.

q: What is the maximum number of instances per deployment in CodeDeploy?

opts.d: No fixed limit, but limited by deployment group instance count

exp.a: Incorrect. There isn't a fixed 100 instance limit.
exp.b: Incorrect. The limit is not fixed at 500.
exp.c: Incorrect. There's no specific 1,000 limit.
exp.d: Correct. CodeDeploy doesn't have a specific hard limit on instances per deployment; it deploys to all instances in the deployment group based on tags or Auto Scaling group membership.

q: A company stores sensitive environment variables for CodeBuild in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store as SecureString parameters. What must be true for CodeBuild to retrieve them?

opts.a: Parameters must be in the same region, and the CodeBuild service role needs ssm:GetParameters permission and kms:Decrypt on the CMK used to encrypt the parameter
opts.b: Only plain text parameters work with CodeBuild
opts.c: Parameters must be stored in Secrets Manager instead
opts.d: CodeBuild automatically has access to all Parameter Store values

exp.a: Correct. The CodeBuild service role needs ssm:GetParameters permission and kms:Decrypt on the KMS key used for SecureString encryption. Parameters must be in the same region as the build project.
exp.b: Incorrect. CodeBuild supports SecureString parameters.
exp.c: Incorrect. Both Parameter Store and Secrets Manager work with CodeBuild.
exp.d: Incorrect. Explicit IAM permissions are required.

q: What is the maximum number of custom action types per account per region in CodePipeline?

exp.a: Incorrect. The limit is higher.
exp.b: Incorrect. 25 is below the limit.
exp.c: Correct. CodePipeline allows a maximum of 50 custom action types per account per region.
exp.d: Incorrect. 100 exceeds the actual limit.

q: A team wants CodeBuild to report test results back to CodePipeline for visualization. What should they configure in buildspec.yml?

opts.a: artifacts section with test output files
opts.b: reports section pointing to test result files (e.g., JUnit XML format)
opts.c: post_build commands to upload to S3

exp.a: Incorrect. Artifacts section is for build output, not test reporting.
exp.b: Correct. The reports section in buildspec.yml specifies test result files in supported formats (JUnit, NUnit, Cucumber, TestNG, Visual Studio TRX) that are published to CodeBuild report groups.
exp.c: Incorrect. Manual S3 upload doesn't integrate with CodeBuild's reporting.
exp.d: Incorrect. The env section doesn't configure test reporting.

q: A CodeDeploy deployment to EC2 instances fails because the appspec.yml has a BeforeInstall hook that times out. What is the default timeout for a lifecycle hook script?

opts.a: 5 minutes
opts.b: 1 hour (3600 seconds)
opts.c: 30 minutes

exp.a: Incorrect. 5 minutes is below the default timeout.
exp.b: Correct. The default timeout for each lifecycle hook script in CodeDeploy is 3600 seconds (1 hour). This can be customized in the appspec.yml file.
exp.c: Incorrect. 30 minutes is not the default.
exp.d: Incorrect. 10 minutes is below the default.

q: What is the maximum timeout you can set for a single lifecycle hook script in CodeDeploy appspec.yml?

opts.a: 1 hour
opts.b: 2 hours
opts.c: 3600 seconds (1 hour, same as default)
opts.d: 3600 seconds (default) but can be set up to 7200 seconds

exp.a: Correct format; 3600 seconds is the maximum per hook.
exp.b: Incorrect. 2 hours exceeds the maximum.
exp.c: Correct. The maximum timeout for a lifecycle event hook is 3600 seconds (1 hour). If you need more time, you should restructure the script.
exp.d: Incorrect. The maximum cannot exceed 3600 seconds per hook.

q: A team uses CodePipeline and wants to deploy to multiple regions simultaneously. How should they configure this?

opts.a: Create a single deploy stage with a cross-region action for each target region
opts.b: Create separate pipelines in each region
opts.c: Use CodeDeploy with multi-region deployment groups
opts.d: Use CloudFormation StackSets instead of CodePipeline

exp.a: Correct. CodePipeline supports cross-region actions. You can add deploy actions in a single stage that target different regions. Each cross-region action uses an artifact bucket in the target region.
exp.b: Incorrect. Separate pipelines add complexity and lack centralized orchestration.
exp.c: Incorrect. CodeDeploy deployment groups don't span multiple regions.
exp.d: Incorrect. While StackSets can deploy cross-region, CodePipeline natively supports cross-region actions.

q: When using CodePipeline cross-region actions, what additional infrastructure is required in the target region?

opts.a: A separate pipeline in the target region
opts.b: An S3 artifact bucket in the target region and a CMK for encryption
opts.c: A VPC in the target region
opts.d: An EC2 instance in the target region

exp.a: Incorrect. A separate pipeline is not needed.
exp.b: Correct. Cross-region actions require an S3 artifact bucket in the target region (created automatically or manually) and an AWS KMS key for artifact encryption in that region.
exp.c: Incorrect. A VPC is not specifically required for cross-region actions.
exp.d: Incorrect. EC2 instances are not required for cross-region pipeline infrastructure.

q: Your organization enforces that all code changes must be reviewed by at least 2 people before merging in CodeCommit. How should you configure this?

opts.a: Create a branch policy blocking direct pushes
opts.b: Create an approval rule template with numberOfApprovalsNeeded set to 2 and associate it with the repository
opts.c: Use IAM policies to deny merge actions
opts.d: Configure a CodeBuild project to check approvals

exp.a: Incorrect. Branch policies alone don't enforce approval counts.
exp.b: Correct. Approval rule templates allow you to set the minimum number of approvals required for pull requests and can be associated with one or more repositories.
exp.c: Incorrect. IAM policies can't easily enforce approval counts.
exp.d: Incorrect. CodeBuild is for building/testing, not enforcing approval workflows.

q: What CodePipeline action category does CodeBuild belong to?

opts.a: Source
opts.b: Build
opts.c: Deploy

exp.a: Incorrect. Source is for code repositories.
exp.b: Correct. CodeBuild is categorized as a Build action provider in CodePipeline. However, it can also be used as a Test action provider.
exp.c: Incorrect. Deploy is for deployment services like CodeDeploy.
exp.d: Incorrect. While CodeBuild can be used for testing, its primary category is Build.

q: A CodeBuild project builds a Node.js application. The build takes 15 minutes, with 10 minutes spent on 'npm install'. How can you reduce build time?

opts.a: Use a larger compute type
opts.b: Enable S3 or local caching for the node_modules directory
opts.c: Remove the install phase

exp.a: Incorrect. Larger compute helps with compilation but npm install is network/IO bound.
exp.b: Correct. Caching the node_modules directory (using S3 or local cache) avoids downloading dependencies on every build, significantly reducing build time.
exp.c: Incorrect. Removing install phase would break the build.
exp.d: Incorrect. CodeBuild uses Docker images, not AMIs.

q: A team accidentally pushed sensitive credentials to a CodeCommit repository. After removing the credentials in a new commit, are the credentials still accessible?

opts.a: No, the new commit permanently removes them
opts.b: Yes, the credentials exist in the Git history and can be accessed by viewing previous commits
opts.c: No, CodeCommit automatically scrubs sensitive data
opts.d: Only administrators can see previous commits

exp.a: Incorrect. Git retains history including previous commit contents.
exp.b: Correct. Even after a new commit removes the credentials, they remain in the Git history. The team should rotate the credentials immediately and consider using git filter-branch or BFG Repo-Cleaner to rewrite history.
exp.c: Incorrect. CodeCommit does not automatically detect or scrub sensitive data.
exp.d: Incorrect. Anyone with read access can view the Git history.

q: What happens when a CodePipeline execution is in QUEUED mode and multiple commits arrive rapidly?

opts.a: Only the latest commit triggers an execution
opts.b: Each commit triggers a separate execution that waits in queue and runs in order
opts.c: All commits are batched into a single execution

exp.a: Incorrect. In QUEUED mode, each trigger creates a separate queued execution.
exp.b: Correct. In QUEUED mode, each source change creates a new execution that waits in queue and executes in FIFO order after the current execution completes.
exp.c: Incorrect. Commits are not batched in QUEUED mode.
exp.d: Incorrect. The pipeline continues to accept triggers.

q: A team is using CodeBuild with a Windows Server build environment. They notice that builds are significantly more expensive than Linux builds. Why?

opts.a: Windows builds have additional licensing fees
opts.b: Windows Server build environments cost more per minute than Linux environments due to licensing costs included in the pricing
opts.c: Windows builds require larger compute types
opts.d: Windows builds take longer due to slower startup

exp.a: Incorrect. There are no separate licensing fees; the cost is included in the per-minute pricing.
exp.b: Correct. Windows Server CodeBuild environments have a higher per-minute cost compared to Linux environments because the Windows licensing cost is included in the build pricing.
exp.c: Incorrect. Windows doesn't require larger compute types.
exp.d: Incorrect. While startup may differ, the cost difference is in per-minute pricing.

q: Your CodeDeploy appspec.yml for a Lambda deployment specifies an AfterAllowTraffic hook pointing to a validation Lambda function. The validation function needs to call CodeDeploy to report success or failure. What API call must the validation function make?

opts.a: codedeploy:UpdateDeploymentGroup
opts.b: codedeploy:PutLifecycleEventHookExecutionStatus
opts.c: codedeploy:StopDeployment

exp.a: Incorrect. This updates deployment group settings, not hook status.
exp.b: Correct. The validation Lambda function must call PutLifecycleEventHookExecutionStatus to report Succeeded or Failed back to CodeDeploy for the lifecycle hook to complete.
exp.c: Incorrect. StopDeployment stops the entire deployment but isn't the hook response mechanism.
exp.d: Incorrect. ContinueDeployment is used for Blue/Green deployments with manual traffic shifting.

q: What CodeBuild feature allows you to store frequently used build environments for faster startup?

opts.a: Warm pools
opts.b: Reserved capacity
opts.c: Build environment cache (Docker layer caching)

exp.a: Incorrect. Warm pools are an Auto Scaling feature, not CodeBuild.
exp.b: Correct. CodeBuild Reserved Capacity (formerly called Fleet) allows you to maintain a set of pre-provisioned build hosts that eliminate cold-start delays and provide faster build startup.
exp.c: Incorrect. Docker layer caching speeds up image builds but doesn't pre-provision environments.
exp.d: Incorrect. The official feature name is Reserved Capacity.
